# Blackwald
**The Blackwald** is a forest in southern [Gilneas](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula "Gilneas peninsula") , located south of [Gilneas City](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Gilneas_City "Gilneas City") and north of [Stormglen Village](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Stormglen_Village "Stormglen Village") .
These woods were the home of the [Druids of the Scythe](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Druids_of_the_Scythe "Druids of the Scythe") , who eventually became the first [worgen](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Worgen "Worgen") .
Tal'doren, also known as "the wild home", is located in the eastern section of the Blackwald in southern Gilneas.
Belysra Starbreeze appears to claim the Druids of the Pack called Tal'doren home in ancient Gilneas.
The Bradshaw Mill is a ruined and abandoned mill located in the southern part of the Blackwald, north of Stormglen Village in Gilneas.
Tempest's Reach is a village and lighthouse on the eastern coast of Gilneas.
Aderic's Repose is a cemetery in Gilneas located outside of the city to the west, not far from Keel Harbor to the north.

# Northgate Woods
The **Northgate Woods** is a forested area in [Gilneas](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula "Gilneas peninsula") , located north of [Gilneas City](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Gilneas_City "Gilneas City") and south of the [Greymane Wall](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Greymane_Wall "Greymane Wall") .
The [Northgate River](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Northgate_River "Northgate River") acts as its eastern border while the road leading to the wall's entrance is its western border. There is no incentive to go here during the [worgen starting experience](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Worgen_starting_experience "Worgen starting experience") .

Here, many human kingdoms, at the age of the Alliance of Lordaeron, that were prosperous, have been found around the lake's shores and nearby mountains, including Lordaeron, Dalaran and Alterac.

The Violet Citadel (or the Violet Tower)[1][2] is the main fortress of Dalaran which housed/houses the Eye of Dalaran, Chamber of Air, research laboratories and great spell libraries of the Kirin Tor — the mage class of Dalaran.
The Kirin Tor's headquarters was the Violet Citadel, an impressive building so named for its stone walls which gave off a faint violet light.

During the Second War, Greymane met with the other human leaders at Capital City to hear of Stormwind's fall at the hands of the orcish Horde. Greymane joined the other human leaders in forming the Alliance of Lordaeron to counter the Horde threat, but due to his pride, he offered only token support.[5]

The [Crowley](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Darius_Crowley) family ruled over the lands that constituted both [Pyrewood Village](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Pyrewood_Village) (and as a result, [Shadowfang Keep](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Shadowfang_Keep)) and [Ambermill](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Ambermill),[4] making [Baron Silverlaine](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Baron_Silverlaine) a vassal of theirs as a result. [Lord Mayor Morrison](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Lord_Mayor_Morrison) was also the mayor of Pyrewood, placing him implicitly under Crowley's service. [Lord Harford](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Lord_Harford) was also noted as a servant of Arugal and from beyond the wall, meaning he was likely one of Crowley's vassals as well. The [Marley](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Lord_Marley) family ruled over an unspecified province near Gilneas' borders, which at the time stretched to about the proximity of the [Deep Elem Mine](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Deep_Elem_Mine). His lands were deemed ill-suited as they lacked natural boundaries to assist with the wall. Given that his lands would not have drawn issue with the Crowleys, his territories were likely near Deep Elem Mine; perhaps [Ambermill](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Ambermill) itself and the surrounding land, which would have made him subservient to Crowley himself. Marley notably remained behind the Greymane Wall in spite of this.

Archibald Greymane was the king of Gilneas and the father of Genn Greymane. Under his rule, Gilneas prospered.
